stories.headline: French police make nearly 1,000 arrests during cost-of-living protests
stories.body:
French police arrested nearly 1,000 people across France during protests on Saturday [c1]. French authorities deployed 70,000 police officers across several cities to manage the crowd [c3]. People protested over the cost of living and school conditions [c3].

Attendance figures differed between the government and trade unions [c2]. The French interior ministry estimated that 410,000 people protested on Saturday [c2]. Trade unions reported about 800,000 participants on the same day [c2]. In Paris, the main protest march drew between 110,000 and 250,000 attendees, according to estimates [c10].

French President Emmanuel Macron decreed that only demonstrations organised by recognised trade unions would be permitted [c4]. French authorities also imposed partial curfews in certain urban zones of Paris and other cities [c8]. Major Paris museums closed on Saturday ahead of scheduled protests [c9]. These closures included the Louvre and the Musée d'Orsay [c9].

French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said two people were seriously injured during the protests [c5]. The serious injuries happened in Toulouse and Clermont-Ferrand [c5]. Nuñez reported a 20-year-old man had his fingers blown off in Toulouse [c11].

Around 550,000 people participated in demonstrations across France the previous weekend [c7]. Those earlier protests resulted in more than 2,500 arrests [c7].

Protests also spread to other European nations on Saturday. Italian police arrested nine people across eight cities during protests [c12]. Italian police also briefly detained 371 others in those cities [c12]. Police said 110 of the people arrested or detained in Italy were minors [c13]. The Italian government deployed 500 soldiers to Milan [c14]. This deployment happened after looting occurred during protests the previous weekend [c14].

Riot police in Tirana, Albania, fired tear gas to disperse thousands of anti-government demonstrators on Saturday [c6].

stories.headline: Ukraine restores Starlink satellite speeds as military operations continue
stories.body:
Ukraine announced on Saturday that its Starlink and Starshield satellite systems returned to full speed [c15]. The systems were restored to pre-restriction operating speeds [c15].

The Ukrainian defence ministry said connectivity remained stable at speeds over 400 kph on Saturday [c19]. Another report from the ministry put the stable speed at more than 250 mph [c25]. Previous restrictions capped Starlink speeds at about 100 mph [c26], or 160 kph [c18]. Ukrainian officials said those speed caps hampered their interception of Russian drones [c18].

SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said on X that Ukraine violated terms by using Starlink for offensive drone strikes [c16]. Ukrainian presidential adviser Serhiy Beskrestnov said Ukraine is physically unable to use Starlink for long and medium range attack drone operations [c17]. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said US President Donald Trump has no role in decisions made by Starlink and Starshield [c20].

Ukrainian forces attacked a chemical plant in the Russian city of Tolyatti on Saturday [c27]. A Russian drone struck a residential building in Kyiv's Obolon District on Saturday, causing a fire [c28]. Trump announced a deal to buy Russian diesel while urging Kyiv to stop striking Russian oil refineries [c21]. Russia agreed to resume three-way negotiations with Washington and Kyiv next month [c23]. Moscow and Kyiv also agreed to a local ceasefire around Oleshky, brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump [c24].

vocab.meaning: stopping or catching something before it arrives

stories.headline: Israel locks down West Bank and demolishes homes in Hebron after shooting
stories.body:
Israel placed the occupied West Bank on lockdown after a shooting attack near Hebron on Friday morning [c29, c30]. Two Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers and injured three others at a checkpoint [c32]. The gunmen were then killed [c32].

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced he reviewed plans for a major West Bank military operation [c33]. He called it the largest operation in the West Bank since 1967 [c33]. Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich called for a comprehensive campaign similar to operations in Gaza and Lebanon [c34]. Smotrich filmed himself wearing body armour in front of a Palestinian building being demolished in Hebron [c36].

Israeli forces demolished homes in the Ein Deir Baha and Farsh al-Hawa neighbourhoods [c31]. Hebron Mayor Yousef al-Ja'bari said 2,200 people were forced from their homes [c37]. Ja'bari also stated more than 1,000 people were displaced by demolitions in those two neighbourhoods [c31]. Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz confirmed about 2,000 people were displaced in Hebron [c38]. The Hebron municipality estimated 35 hectares were destroyed or marked for destruction in Ein Deir Baha [c35].

Israeli forces arrested about 70 Palestinians during raids across at least 15 areas of the West Bank [c40]. Forces fired a stun grenade at Al Jazeera journalists near the Farsh al-Hawa checkpoint [c39].

vocab.meaning: forced to leave the place where you live

stories.headline: Gunmen open fire at church funeral in Jordan, killing up to nine people
stories.body:
Gunmen attacked St George's Greek Orthodox church during a funeral in Hamoud, Jordan [c41]. Nine people were killed in the shooting, according to initial reports [c41]. Reuters later updated the death toll from the shooting to eight people killed [c48]. Jordan's health minister reported that 40 people were injured [c42].

The church is located in Karak, about 90 kilometers south of Jordan's capital, Amman [c46]. Security camera footage showed three attackers firing at the church entrance [c43]. The attackers took cover behind trees and a low wall [c43].

Jordanian Prime Minister Jafar Hassan said on X that the attack resulted from a terrorist ideology and blind extremism [c44]. King Abdullah II visited Karak after the attack [c45]. King Abdullah promised the perpetrators would be punished with an iron fist [c45]. Jordan declared three days of national mourning after the church attack [c47].

Indian External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar condemned the church attack [c49]. Jaishankar expressed solidarity with the Jordanian government and people [c49].

vocab.meaning: people who carry out a harmful or illegal act

stories.headline: Brazilian presidential candidates hold final rallies ahead of run-off vote
stories.body:
Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva addressed supporters at Copacabana Beach on the final day of campaigning [c52]. City Hall estimated that about 1.1 million people attended the beach rally in Rio de Janeiro [c57]. Lula also attended a large rally on Paulista Avenue in São Paulo on Saturday afternoon [c58].

Nearly 159 million Brazilians are eligible to vote in the presidential election run-off on Sunday [c56]. Senator Flávio Bolsonaro defeated incumbent President Lula in the first round of the election on October 4 [c50]. Flávio Bolsonaro received 47 percent of the vote in that round, compared to Lula's 45 percent [c53].

Flávio Bolsonaro is the son of imprisoned former president Jair Bolsonaro [c51]. The elder Bolsonaro is serving a 27-year prison sentence for attempting a coup after losing the 2022 election [c55].

A survey released on Saturday showed Flávio Bolsonaro leading with 46.3 percent against Lula's 45 percent [c54]. During campaign rallies, Flávio Bolsonaro said he will join Donald Trump's Shield of the Americas regional security initiative if elected [c59].

stories.headline: Bay of Bengal weather system threatens South India with heavy rain and landslides
stories.body:
The India Meteorological Department reported that a low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal persisted on October 23 [c60]. On Saturday evening, the depression lay centered about 510 km off the Andaman Islands [c82]. It was also 820 km off the Visakhapatnam coast [c82].

The weather agency warned that the low-pressure area is expected to intensify into a cyclonic storm by October 26 [c76]. The agency issued a red alert for 13 districts in Andhra Pradesh for October 27 and 28 [c83]. Officials advised fisherfolk not to venture into the sea from October 26 onwards [c78]. Last year's cyclone Montha was classified as a severe cyclonic storm [c63]. A very severe cyclonic storm carries maximum sustained wind speeds between 118 km/h and 221 km/h [c80]. During cyclone Montha, the wind speed recorded at Machilipatnam reached 65 km/h [c81].

Heavy rain triggered landslides and damage in southern India. Overnight rainfall caused landslides at more than 10 locations along the Coonoor-Mettupalayam National Highway [c68]. A landslide struck near Barliyar on the Mettupalayam-Ooty road [c69]. Government bus driver Janakaraj died, and conductor Kesavan was injured when mud and trees buried their bus near Burliar [c62, c69]. A house in Barliyar village was completely washed away by rainfall, but its occupants escaped unharmed [c71]. A goods vehicle carrying chickens was swept into a gorge during a landslide, though its driver escaped unhurt [c70].

Local officials took emergency action across affected areas. Nilgiris District Collector Lakshmi Bhavya Tanneeru advised people to avoid traveling on affected roads unless necessary [c73]. The Nilgiris district administration set up emergency helpline 1077 for residents [c74]. Stranded bus passengers were evacuated to relief camps in Coonoor [c72]. In Puliyampatti, heavy rains flooded a Sri Lankan Tamil refugee camp, inundating more than 100 houses [c65]. District Collector S. Durga Moorthy visited the camp to assess the damage [c66].

The weather system is affecting multiple regions across India. The Northeast monsoon has set in over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, and other southern regions [c75]. The weather agency predicted moderate to heavy rainfall across Tamil Nadu and Puducherry until October 26 [c61]. Coastal and western districts of West Bengal expect heavy rainfall starting October 28 [c77]. Thunderstorms with wind gusts up to 40 km per hour are expected over south Bengal districts [c79]. The Odisha government announced the closure of schools and colleges in five districts on October 28 and 29 [c64]. Telangana is experiencing a rainfall deficit and drinking water shortages due to El Nino [c67].

vocab.meaning: flooding or covering completely with water
the amount by which something is too small or lacking
